notes: Normal tier, urban setting only. Targets balance.normal.urban.min, which batch 005 left failing at 18.1% against a 25% floor — the only gate a Normal batch can currently improve. Every coordinate names a specific central street, commercial avenue, square or transit corridor in a mid-sized or lesser-known city, chosen so the view is readable but not identifiable on sight. Countries with demonstrated verification success are preferred; Kenya is excluded. Maximum 3 per country. No panoId appears here: one may only come from a real verification run.

candidates.label: Zhongzheng Road, Hsinchu
candidates.source: Central commercial street through Hsinchu's downtown core.
candidates.rationale: Normal, not easy: traditional Chinese shopfront signage and scooter traffic place it in Taiwan or coastal China for a player who reads the script, but nothing identifies Hsinchu. Taipei 101 is the only Taiwanese view in the catalog that gives itself away; this one gives nothing.

candidates.label: Wenhua Road, Chiayi
candidates.source: Chiayi's main night-market and commercial street.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a dense low-rise commercial street with vertical signage. The clue set is script, road markings and utility poles — enough to reach the country, not the city.

candidates.label: Zhongshan Road, Hualien
candidates.source: Principal avenue through central Hualien, on Taiwan's east coast.
candidates.rationale: Normal: wider and greener than the west-coast cities, with mountains sometimes visible at the end of the street. That is a hint toward eastern Taiwan for an attentive player, which is what normal should reward — a solvable inference, not a giveaway.

candidates.label: Dongseong-ro, Daegu
candidates.source: Daegu's central shopping and transit corridor.
candidates.rationale: Normal: hangul signage settles the country immediately, so the round turns on distinguishing a large provincial city from Seoul. No palace, tower or bridge appears.

candidates.label: Gaeksa-gil, Jeonju
candidates.source: Gaeksa-gil, the commercial street in central Jeonju, deliberately away from the hanok village.
candidates.rationale: Normal rather than easy precisely because the coordinate avoids the hanok quarter — the traditional roofs a few hundred metres away would be a strong visual tell. An ordinary Korean shopping street is not.

candidates.label: Myeongdong street, Chuncheon
candidates.source: Chuncheon's central Myeongdong shopping street.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a mid-sized inland city with hills behind the rooflines. Same reasoning as Daegu — country readable, city not.

candidates.label: J.M. Basa Street, Iloilo City
candidates.source: Calle Real (J.M. Basa Street), Iloilo City's heritage commercial street.
candidates.rationale: Normal: Spanish-era commercial facades with English-language signage and jeepneys. The combination narrows to the Philippines but not to Iloilo, and Intramuros — the catalog's other Philippine city entry — looks nothing like it.

candidates.label: Lacson Street, Bacolod
candidates.source: Lacson Street, the main commercial corridor of Bacolod.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a wide modern provincial avenue. Tricycles, English signage and tropical planting give the country; nothing gives the island.

candidates.label: Session Road, Baguio
candidates.source: Session Road, the central sloping avenue of Baguio.
candidates.rationale: Normal: pines and a steep gradient contradict the tropical-lowland reading, which is a genuine inference to make rather than a memorised landmark. 250 km from Vigan, so it does not crowd that cluster.

candidates.label: Horní náměstí, Olomouc
candidates.source: Horní náměstí, the upper square of Olomouc.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a Central European baroque square with Czech signage. Prague's old town is instantly recognisable and sits in the catalog as easy; Olomouc's square is the same architecture with none of the recognition.

candidates.label: náměstí Republiky, Plzeň
candidates.source: náměstí Republiky, the central square of Plzeň.
candidates.rationale: Normal: gothic church tower over a coloured burgher square — regionally typical, individually anonymous. Czech street signs are the strongest clue available.

candidates.label: Velké náměstí, Hradec Králové
candidates.source: Velké náměstí, the upper town square of Hradec Králové.
candidates.rationale: Normal: same reasoning as Plzeň, and 120 km from it, so the two do not share a cluster.

candidates.label: ulica Piotrkowska, Łódź
candidates.source: ulica Piotrkowska, the long central axis of Łódź.
candidates.rationale: Normal: nineteenth-century industrial-era tenements, Polish signage, tram infrastructure. Kraków's main square is the catalog's easy Polish view; a Łódź tenement street is its opposite.

candidates.label: ulica Gdańska, Bydgoszcz
candidates.source: ulica Gdańska, the main north-south street of central Bydgoszcz.
candidates.rationale: Normal: an ordinary Polish provincial city street with trams and mixed pre-war and post-war frontage. Nothing distinguishes it from a dozen similar cities, which is the point.

candidates.label: Krakowskie Przedmieście, Lublin
candidates.source: Krakowskie Przedmieście, Lublin's central pedestrian and commercial avenue.
candidates.rationale: Normal: eastern Poland reads slightly differently from the west — lower buildings, wider street — which a strong player can use. The old town gate a few hundred metres east was avoided deliberately.

candidates.label: Raekoja plats, Tartu
candidates.source: Raekoja plats, the town hall square of Tartu.
candidates.rationale: Normal: pastel neoclassical facades and Estonian signage. The language is the whole clue, and it is a small language — a fair normal round, well short of Tallinn's recognisable skyline.

candidates.label: Puškini street, Narva
candidates.source: Puškini street, the central avenue of Narva.
candidates.rationale: Normal, and an unusually instructive one: Narva is Estonian but overwhelmingly Russian-speaking, so a player reading the shop signs will guess Russia and land 5 km short across the river. That is the kind of near-miss a normal round should produce.

candidates.label: Tallinna street, Viljandi
candidates.source: Tallinna street, central Viljandi.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a small Baltic county town, wooden and stucco buildings, Estonian signage. 90 km from Tartu and 80 km from Pärnu, so all three sit in separate clusters.

candidates.label: Gran Vía del Rey Juan Carlos I, Logroño
candidates.source: Gran Vía, the main boulevard of Logroño in La Rioja.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a mid-century Spanish provincial boulevard — plane trees, apartment blocks, Spanish signage. Barcelona's Sagrada Família is the catalog's easy Spanish view; this is a street that could be any of forty Spanish cities.

candidates.label: Avenida 2, Cartago
candidates.source: Avenida 2 through central Cartago.
candidates.rationale: Normal: low concrete commercial frontage with mountains behind, Spanish signage, Central American vehicle mix. 19 km from the San José entry, so the cluster holds two groups against a limit of three.

candidates.label: Avenida Central, Liberia
candidates.source: Avenida Central, the main street of Liberia in Guanacaste.
candidates.rationale: Normal: dry-tropical Guanacaste looks nothing like the central valley — browner, flatter, lower. A player who knows Costa Rica can use that; a player who does not still reaches Central America.

candidates.label: Avenida Juárez, Puebla
candidates.source: Avenida Juárez, the main commercial avenue west of Puebla's centre.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a modern Mexican city avenue, chosen instead of Puebla's tiled colonial centre, which would have been an easy round. 100 km from the Mexico City entry.

candidates.label: Calle del Sol, Santiago de los Caballeros
candidates.source: Calle del Sol, the central commercial street of Santiago de los Caballeros.
candidates.rationale: Normal: dense Caribbean commercial frontage, Spanish signage, no coastline. Santo Domingo's colonial zone is the catalog's recognisable Dominican view; this is 155 km inland from it.

candidates.label: Main Street, Moncton
candidates.source: Main Street through downtown Moncton, New Brunswick.
candidates.rationale: Normal: bilingual English and French signage on a small Atlantic-Canadian main street. The bilingualism points at Canada without pointing at Quebec, which is a real distinction to make rather than a memorised view.

candidates.label: Avenida Higienópolis, Londrina
candidates.source: Avenida Higienópolis, central Londrina, Paraná.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a planned mid-century interior city — wide avenue, modern blocks, Portuguese signage. Nothing like Copacabana or Pelourinho, the catalog's two recognisable Brazilian views.

candidates.label: Rua do Príncipe, Joinville
candidates.source: Rua do Príncipe, the main commercial street of Joinville, Santa Catarina.
candidates.rationale: Normal: southern Brazil with visible German settlement influence, which contradicts the tropical default and gives a strong player something to work with. 330 km from Curitiba's outskirts entry.

candidates.label: Calle Balcarce, Salta
candidates.source: Calle Balcarce, north of Salta's centre.
candidates.rationale: Normal: northwest Argentina — low colonial-influenced frontage, dry hills at the end of the street. Distinct from the Buenos Aires obelisk, which is the catalog's easy Argentine view, and 900 km from the Córdoba entry.

candidates.label: Avenida Alemania, Temuco
candidates.source: Avenida Alemania, Temuco, in Chile's Araucanía region.
candidates.rationale: Normal: southern Chilean city — steeper roofs, more rain-adapted building than the centre or north. Valparaíso's hills and Santiago's centre are both far more identifiable.

candidates.label: Carrera 27, Bucaramanga
candidates.source: Carrera 27, a main north-south corridor through Bucaramanga.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a modern Andean-foothill city, mid-rise and green. Cartagena's walled city is the recognisable Colombian view; this is 55 km from the Barichara entry and looks nothing like it.

candidates.label: Avenida España, Trujillo
candidates.source: Avenida España, the ring avenue around central Trujillo.
candidates.rationale: Normal: coastal desert light and dense low commercial frontage. The Plaza de Armas two blocks inside would have been an easy round; the ring road is not.

candidates.label: Calle Bolívar, Loja
candidates.source: Calle Bolívar, central Loja in southern Ecuador.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a southern Andean provincial city, far from the catalog's Quito and Cuenca entries — 380 km and 190 km respectively — and with no monument in frame.

candidates.label: Maitland Street, Bloemfontein
candidates.source: Maitland Street through central Bloemfontein.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a dry interior South African city centre. English and Afrikaans signage narrows the country quickly, so the difficulty sits in placing it inland rather than on either coast.

candidates.label: Oxford Street, East London
candidates.source: Oxford Street, the main commercial street of East London, Eastern Cape.
candidates.rationale: Normal: mid-century commercial frontage on the Indian Ocean coast, 800 km from Cape Town and 250 km from Graaff-Reinet. No mountain or harbour gives the location away.

candidates.label: Commercial Street, Cape Coast
candidates.source: Commercial Street in central Cape Coast, away from the castle.
candidates.rationale: Normal: West African coastal town commerce with English signage. The castle 500 m south would have been a landmark round; the coordinate stays on the commercial street on purpose. 60 km from the Takoradi N1 entry.

candidates.label: KN 4 Avenue, Kigali
candidates.source: KN 4 Avenue through central Kigali.
candidates.rationale: Normal: unusually clean and hilly for an African capital, with distinctive alphanumeric street naming — real clues that reward knowledge rather than recall. The catalog's other two Rwandan entries are both rural.

candidates.label: Rue Maréchal Leclerc, Saint-Denis
candidates.source: Rue Maréchal Leclerc, central Saint-Denis de La Réunion.
candidates.rationale: Normal, and a good trap: French signage, French road furniture and tropical vegetation together. A player who reads only the language lands in mainland France. 25 km from the Cilaos road entry, which is mountain rather than city.

candidates.label: Sturt Street, Ballarat
candidates.source: Sturt Street, the central boulevard of Ballarat, Victoria.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a wide gold-rush-era boulevard with a planted median. Left-hand traffic and eucalypts give the hemisphere and country; nothing gives the state. Well clear of Melbourne's Flinders Street entry at 105 km.

candidates.label: Flinders Street, Townsville
candidates.source: Flinders Street through central Townsville, Queensland.
candidates.rationale: Normal: tropical north Queensland — palms, verandahs, harsh light. The contrast with the southern cities is a genuine inference, and 1100 km separates it from the Brisbane entry.

candidates.label: Charles Street, Launceston
candidates.source: Charles Street, central Launceston, Tasmania.
candidates.rationale: Normal: Georgian and Victorian brick in a cool-temperate climate — plausibly New Zealand or southern Australia, which is exactly the kind of two-way choice normal should pose. Tasmania failed once in batch 001, but that was a rural highway; this is a city street.

candidates.label: Marine Parade, Napier
candidates.source: Marine Parade, Napier, Hawke's Bay. Chosen over the pedestrianised Emerson Street one block inland.
candidates.rationale: Normal: art-deco frontage facing a Pacific shoreline. Distinctive enough to be solvable, obscure enough that only a player who knows Napier's 1931 rebuild will place it. 320 km from Wellington and 200 km from Rotorua.
